Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray and CT images demonstrate a reticulonodular pattern that is predominantly distributed in the upper lung fields, along with a left-sided pleural effusion (visible as blunting of the left costophrenic angle on the X-ray and fluid collection on the lower CT slice). This specific combination of upper-zone predominant interstitial disease and unilateral effusion is characteristic of Pulmonary Langerhans' Cell Histiocytosis (LCH), whereas heart failure and pulmonary edema typically present with lower zone predominance and bilateral findings.
